newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-GENTLE START TO TITLE DEFENCE FOR ZAMALEK.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GENTLE START TO TITLE DEFENCE FOR ZAMALEK.

text.p: Zamalek start the defence of their African Champions Cup title in Cairo on Friday with a seemingly easy tie against Ethiopia's St George.

But the Egyptian club, chasing a fifth African title, will be mindful of the inability of their country's national team to beat Ethiopian opposition in an African Nations Cup qualifying tie last month.

The Egyptian team, dominated by Zamalek players, was held to a draw by weaker opposition, giving a major morale boost to Ethiopian soccer which has traditionally been on the receiving end of some severe footballing lessons from Egyptian opposition.
Zamalek, who added the African Super Cup to their packed mantlepiece last month, will field the same squad that won a record fourth Champions Cup title in December.
The match is among a packed programme of first round, first leg matches in the three African club competitions this weekend.

Zamalek head the list of favourites chasing places in the eight-team African Champions League, which will start in September. Instead of the traditional knockout format of the competition, the last eight teams will be divided into two groups of four once the competition is past the second round stage.

The Confederation of African Football (CAF) have introduced the new formula in an attempt to emulate the financial and marketing success achieve in Europe since the traditional format of the European Cup was changed and the European Champions League introduced.
This year's field has several former winners, including Algeria's Mouloudia Alger, Raja Casablanca of Morocco, Tunisia's Club Africain and Orlando Pirates of South Africa.

Like Zamalek, all are expected to have relatively trouble-free paths into the second round in May. Mouloudia Alger host Desportivo Travadores of the Cape Verde Islands while Raja are at home to Senegal's Sonacos de Diourbel.
Club Africain meet Mali's Djoliba in Tunis while Pirates play against Lesotho's Roma Rovers in Johannesburg on Sunday.
The South African team are the only non-north African team to have won the competition in the last 14 years.
In the African Cup Winners' Cup, Arab Contractors begin the defence of their title away in Kenya against Mumias Sugar.
The Cairo team are seeking to emulate Egyptian compatriots Al Ahli and become only the second team to win the Cup Winners' Cup four times.
Kawkab Marakesh of Morocco, who won last year's CAF Cup, meet ASC la Linguere of Senegal in their first round, first leg match at home this Sunday.
